$comment: Pinned model/provider configuration for the PyJWT bounded-task rule-generation pilot (Arms C/D only -- see protocol.md#9-model-provider-selection). Real, frozen decision; zero calls have been made against it. Consumed by console/panels/llmAttempts.js and console/panels/costUsage.js.
status: configured, not yet executed -- blocked on a billable API key and explicit spend authorization (see protocol.md#10-real-pilot-execution-status)
scope: PyJWT 1->2 bounded task only (the 'first PyJWT pilot' this pass was asked to close). SQLAlchemy and Pydantic pilot generation configs are NOT decided by this pass.
api: Messages API (https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages), direct x-api-key auth -- not the Claude Code session's own auth token, which is not an appropriate credential for an independently-logged, separately-billed research measurement
model_id_pinning_note: Exact dated snapshot ID, not an alias like 'claude-haiku-4-5-latest'. Roadmap requires a pinned, reproducible model/provider configuration shared across arms A-D; recording the snapshot ID lets every request be traced to a fixed model version even though the roadmap's own glossary notes temperature=0 does not guarantee bit-identical hosted output.
why_this_model: Cheapest current Claude model per published pricing (see price_schedule below) -- minimizes real spend across the 1/2/3/5 repair-proposal sweep and multiple generation replicates, satisfying 'inexpensive' and 'do not spend unnecessarily'.
Same family/API used for baselines keeps Arms A-D in one monetary/tokenization system, satisfying the roadmap's 'comparable monetary units' requirement without a cross-provider exchange assumption.

Messages API usage object reports uncached input tokens, cache creation (write) tokens, cache read tokens, and output tokens directly on every response -- satisfies the roadmap's required per-request ledger fields (ROADMAP.md#economics-and-prompt-caching) with no extra instrumentation.
Supports prompt caching with published, dated per-token cache write/read prices, needed because the repair sweep reuses one evidence-packet prefix across up to 5 requests per replicate.

Fast/low-latency, appropriate for a small bounded-DSL JSON-generation task; a larger/more expensive model (Sonnet 5, Opus 5) is not justified by this pilot's task size and would inflate cost with no identified benefit for a 2-operation rule bundle.

rejected_alternatives.reason: 5-25x more expensive per the same price schedule; no evidence this bounded 2-operation task needs the extra capability. Registered as the model to reconsider only if Haiku 4.5 demonstrably fails to produce schema-plausible output across replicates.

Would introduce a second pricing schedule and a different tokenizer, complicating same-monetary-units comparison across arms for no identified benefit at pilot scale. Not ruled out for later phases, e.g. an explicit cross-provider ablation.

request_parameters.temperature_caveat: Recorded per glossary.md's Temperature entry: 0 reduces but does not guarantee reproducible hosted output. Every request's response `id`, model version, and timestamp will be logged regardless.
request_parameters.max_output_tokens_rationale: Generous margin over the ~300-600 token estimated output size (pilot_estimate.json) while still bounding worst-case per-request spend; an output hitting this cap is logged as a truncation failure, not silently accepted.
request_parameters.response_mode: tool_use with a single forced tool named `emit_rule_bundle` whose input_schema mirrors the informal shape in pilot_evidence_packet.md -- 'a constrained provider response mode where available' per ROADMAP.md Phase 3, always re-validated locally rather than trusted.

caching_policy.cache_breakpoint: the combined system prompt + evidence packet (pilot_evidence_packet.md), placed in the stable prefix per ROADMAP.md's caching-prefix policy
caching_policy.cache_type: Anthropic default ephemeral (5-minute TTL) cache -- realistic default availability, not a purchased extended-retention tier; will be disclosed if it changes

price_schedule.note: Fetched live this pass via WebFetch; this is a real, dated, publicly-published price schedule, not an estimate -- the ROADMAP's requirement to record 'price schedule date' is satisfied even though no request has been billed against it yet.

generation_replicates_rationale: Resolves protocol.md's previously-open 'numeric replicate counts beyond a small number, policy TBD' for the PyJWT pilot specifically. 2 is the minimum count that can distinguish a single-generation fluke from any repeatable behavior at all, at roughly double (not 10x or 100x) the cost of 1. Registered here BEFORE any generation call is made, so it cannot be chosen using outcome data. Does not resolve SQLAlchemy/Pydantic replicate counts, which need their own registration before their pilots run.
repair_proposal_sweep_source: ROADMAP.md#development-set-repair-policy and protocol.md#5, restated here, not newly decided
repair_trajectory_policy: paired-prefix: one generation replicate = one trajectory of up to 5 sequential requests sharing the cached evidence-packet prefix; budgets 1/2/3/5 are read off prefixes of that one trajectory, per protocol.md#5's 'avoid confounding budget with unrelated initial generations' -- NOT 1+2+3+5=11 independent generations per replicate.

retry_and_timeout_policy.policy_note: This is a frozen CAP set by policy before any call is made, per ROADMAP.md's 'transport retries must also be capped' -- it is not derived from observed retry behavior, because no request has been made yet. A request exceeding the timeout or retry cap is logged as an infrastructure failure, not silently retried indefinitely.
retry_and_timeout_policy.semantic_vs_transport: A malformed/invalid JSON response counts as a used proposal in the repair sweep (a semantic attempt), never as a free transport retry.
